title: MIT LiON Deep Learning Screens 1.6M Lipids to Discover Pulmonary mRNA Gene-Therapy Nanoparticles
shortTitle: MIT LiON: AI Pulmonary mRNA Lipids
whyItMatters: Published in Nature Biotechnology: trained on >9,000 LNP measurements, LiON screened 1.6 million ionizable lipids to discover FO-32 and FO-35—achieving potent nebulized mRNA delivery in mouse and ferret lungs.
summary: MIT researchers led by Daniel G. Anderson and Robert Langer (with the University of Iowa) introduced LiON (Lipid Optimization using Neural Networks) in Nature Biotechnology to break the liver-targeting bottleneck of non-viral mRNA delivery. Generating a dataset of >9,000 lipid nanoparticle activity measurements to train a directed message-passing neural network, the team screened 1.6 million virtual lipids and extrapolated to structurally divergent chemical families—discovering two novel ionizable lipids, FO-32 and FO-35, that delivered nebulized mRNA efficiently into mouse and ferret lungs (a key preclinical model for cystic fibrosis gene therapy).
technicalHighlights: Trained a directed message-passing graph neural network (LiON) on >9,000 experimental lipid nanoparticle activity measurements.
Screened 1.6 million candidate ionizable lipids in silico, generalizing accurately to structurally novel lipid chemistries outside the training distribution.
Discovered FO-32 and FO-35, achieving state-of-the-art nebulized mRNA delivery in mouse lungs and efficient pulmonary mRNA delivery in ferrets.
caveats: Demonstrated in preclinical mouse and ferret models; human clinical safety, repeat-dosing tolerability, and GMP manufacturing remain to be established.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates deep graph neural networks extrapolating across chemical space to solve extra-hepatic organ-targeted nucleic-acid delivery.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly advances inhaled mRNA and CRISPR gene therapies for cystic fibrosis, asthma, and pulmonary diseases.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature Biotechnology with extensive in vitro assays and in vivo validation in both mice and ferrets.
scoreRationale.velocity: Evaluated 1.6 million candidate lipids computationally to uncover two high-potency pulmonary delivery vehicles.

sources.label: Witten, Raji, Langer, Anderson et al. — Artificial intelligence-guided design of lipid nanoparticles for pulmonary gene therapy (Nature Biotechnology, 2024/2025)
